Broncos vs. Rams picks, prediction, player props: Expert's best bets for Sunday Night Football in NFL Week 3 Mile High altitude and a stout Denver defense give the underdog hosts a distinct edge against Los Angeles in a tight prime-time battle By Will Brinson Sep 27, 2026 at 8:07 pm ET • 3 min read Add CBS Sports on Google Imagn Images The NFL never disappoints, and Week 3 of the 2026 season appears to be no different. Just when we think we know everything, we know very little. Sunday Night Football will be a good test of how little we know, with the Broncos playing Jekyll and Hyde the first two weeks of the season and in the two different halves against the Jaguars last week. The total is down to 44.5. Bet on Sunday Night Football at DraftKings, where new users get $150 in bonus bets after they spend $5+: The Rams pulled a similar move in Week 1 versus Week 2, and now they're favored on the road in prime time in a really tough place to play early in the year. They opened with a loss to the 49ers but bounced back by cruising past the Giants 28-6 on Monday night in Week 2. Los Angeles is a 1.5-point favorite, and the Over/Under for total points is 44.5. Get a $55 bonus after $25 in trades by claiming the latest Kalshi promo code CBSSPORTS55 here : Best bets for Sunday Night Football Broncos +2.5 I'm *the* Rams guy -- we joked about what the number would need to be in order for me to NOT take the Rams on our SportsLine picks show Wednesday. And I was on the Rams earlier in the week, but I'm pivoting now, with me thinking the altitude plus the Broncos defense and the high level of this Denver team meaning that the Broncos probably shouldn't be underdogs at home this early in the year. Aaron Donald returned to the NFL last week and played a decent number of snaps, but it's going to be tough for him to ramp up at Mile High. Sean Payton can coach around the weaknesses of his team, and while I expect the Rams to very much keep this competitive and for it to a be a low-scoring close game, my spidey sense says the Broncos find a way to win late, and if not, it's a field goal walk-off situation for either team, making these points extremely valuable. Sunday Night Football player props Jaylen Waddle 6+ receptions (+127, DraftKings) You'll see the Over for Waddle's receptions above heavily juiced, but just know that we're playing his SIX reception number at +127 on DraftKings here. I like both, obviously, and think this is a good ladder spot for Waddle. In Week 1 he was non-existent, which is shocking given that the Broncos traded a first-round pick for him this offseason. Week 2 was very different and the Broncos reaped the benefits. I fully expect Davis Webb and Sean Payton to get Waddle heavily involved, especially since the Broncos running back depth chart is extremely depleted. Kyren Williams over 12.5 receiving yards (-116, DraftKings) Williams and Blake Corum are very much in a timeshare at running back at this point and I don't think that will change. It makes backing their rush props difficult. But it also means Williams receiving prop is way down. He's always good for several targets in the short-yardage area and 12.5 isn't that much to ask from the standout running back, especially when Denver's ability to bring pressure plus the likely absence of Puka Nacua meaning safety valves for Matthew Stafford will likely be a play-calling focus for McVay. Bet on NFL player props and more at BetMGM: Sunday Night Football anytime touchdowns Davante Adams (+115, DraftKings) Davante went off in Week 2 after a slow Week 1, and while this matchup is much more difficult for the superstar wide receiver, he's getting a fantastic price here on an anytime touchdown. The Broncos and Patrick Surtain will make life difficult, and I definitely don't see him chasing 200 receiving yards. But at plus money with his usage and red-zone scoring ability? This is a no-brainer. Bo Nix (+475, DraftKings) This number has me giddy! Bo Nix is almost 5-1 to score a touchdown??? Yeah the Rams defense is great and yeah Nix hasn't been running like we'd prefer with eight rushes for eight total yards. But he's always a threat to run and against this defense I think he'll take off a few more times. And I actually foresee some red-zone dial ups to activate his legs in tough spots, making this number extremely tantalizing. His first-touchdown-scorer number of 18-1 is real nice as well. An NFL player prop is a bet on how an individual player will perform in a game. Instead of betting on the winner, point spread, or total score, you're betting on a specific outcome or statistic for that player. Common NFL player props include: Passing yards, completions, attempts, and passing touchdowns (quarterbacks). Rushing yards and rushing attempts (running backs, quarterbacks, and other rushers). Receptions and receiving yards (wide receivers, tight ends, and running backs). Anytime, first, and multiple touchdown scorers (eligible offensive players and defenses/special teams). Most player props are offered as over/under bets. For example, a sportsbook might set a quarterback's passing yards at 245.5. You can bet the over if you think he'll finish with 246 or more, or the under if you think he'll finish with 245 or fewer. Touchdown scorer props work differently: you’re simply betting whether a player scores, with the odds reflecting the sportsbook's assessment of how likely that is. One thing that makes player props different from game bets is how much they depend on the game script. A team that falls behind by three scores is likely to throw more and run less, which can boost passing and receiving opportunities while cutting into rushing volume. That's why our projections account for the expected game script when estimating how a player is likely to perform. We also incorporate advanced metrics and play-by-play data. From projection to probability : We run simulations of the upcoming game to estimate how often a player finishes over or under the specific line being offered. That gives us the probability shown on the board. Probability meets price : We compare our projected probability with the probability implied by the sportsbook's odds. articles.text: Week 1 NFL Player Props: Best Prop Bets & Predictions Skip to content Purchase Watch & Listen Login Dashboard Betting Fantasy Analysis Props Stats Content Sportsbook Newsletter Betting Fantasy Analysis Props Stats Content Sportsbook Newsletter Betting Week 1 NFL Player Props: Best Prop Bets & Predictions By Josh Shepardson | 2026-09-13T09:01:27-04:00 Sep 13, 2026 | View Larger Image NFL Best Prop Bets: Week 1 Picks Christian Watson Over 55.5 Receiving Yards (-110) Juwan Johnson Over 41.5 Receiving Yards (-110) Chase Brown Over 23.5 Receiving Yards (-111) Sharp Betting Tools: NFL Props: Lines & Odds NFL Spreads, Totals, & Moneylines NFL Weather Forecast & Potential Impact NFL Implied Team Totals NFL Week 1 Best Prop Bet: Christian Watson Over 55.5 Receiving Yards (-110) Watson tore his ACL on January 5, 2025, in Week 18 of the 2024 season. He made his season debut last year on October 26, 2025, in Week 8. Remarkably, Watson didn't skip a beat. In fact, he played the best football of his career. The speedster can get off to a fast start this year, and the Packers might lean into the passing attack more while sorting through their backfield with Josh Jacobs on the Commissioner's Exempt List. The matchup against the Vikings could also prompt them to pass more. Per TruMedia, the Vikings were tied for 12th in expected points added (EPA) allowed per designed rush in 2025 and fifth in yards before contact allowed per rush attempt (1.05). Minnesota's coverage tendencies also boost Watson's receiving outlook. According to the Fantasy Points Data Suite 2.0, the Vikings were first in two-high coverage rate (69.0%) and first in blitz rate (44.7%) in 2025. Watson rattled off a 20% target rate per route and 2.42 yards per route run (Y/RR) on 119 routes against two-high coverage in 2025. Furthermore, he had a 26% target rate per route and 2.47 Y/RR on 77 routes against the blitz last season, reeling in 10 receptions on 20 targets for 190 receiving yards. Watson exceeded 55.5 receiving yards only five times in 11 games in 2025. That said, the Packers have thinned their wide receiving corps, and Watson should exceed last year's 68.6% route participation rate in a less crowded wideout room. On a more expansive route participation rate, with a possible uptick in the Packers' passing rate from last year's 24th ranking in pass rate over expected (-2.1% PROE) out of the gate, Watson should clear 55.5 receiving yards. NFL Week 1 Best Prop Bet: Juwan Johnson Over 41.5 Receiving Yards (-110) Kellen Moore brought his fast-paced brand of offense to the Saints last year. New Orleans played at the NFL's fastest pace in 2025, which is favorable for play volume. The Saints were only 19th in PROE (-0.6%), but their passing tendencies ratcheted up down the stretch. In the final four weeks of the regular season, New Orleans was tied for third in PROE (5.0%). They did play the Titans during those four weeks, and Tennessee's defense faced an NFL-high 6.4% PROE. However, the Saints also played the Panthers, Jets, and Falcons in that period, and they ranked 25th (-1.6%), 21st (-0.3%), and 20th (0.3%), respectively, in PROE faced in the 2025 regular season. The Saints had a banged-up backfield at that point, but Moore's willingness to cut Tyler Shough loose can also be viewed as bullish for his trust in the young quarterback. Speaking of Shough, Johnson excelled with the rookie quarterback. In 10 games that Shough played at least 20 snaps last season, Johnson recorded a 71.3% route participation rate, 16.2% target share, 20% target rate per route, 17.7% air yards share, 8.9-yard average depth of target (aDOT), 4.6 receptions per game, 57.4 receiving yards per game, and 1.97 Y/RR. The pass-catching tight end cleared 41.5 receiving yards in five of his last eight games last year. That includes the final three, when he ripped off 89, 95, and 61 receiving yards. Johnson can pick up where he left off for the Saints, and with New Orleans serving as one of the week's biggest underdogs, he should be in a negative gamescript, necessitating the Saints air it out to keep up with Detroit's high-powered offense. NFL Week 1 Best Prop Bet: Chase Brown Over 23.5 Receiving Yards (-111) I'm not on an island on the Sharp Football Analysis team for this pick. Rich Hribar shouted out Brown over 23.5 receiving yards on the NFL Week 1 Best Bets & Player Props Show . A top-down view is immediately favorable for Brown's receiving outlook. Since 2023, the Bengals are tied for first in PROE (7.9%). Conversely, the Buccaneers have been the NFL's biggest pass funnel since 2023, facing the highest PROE (4.3%). The Bengals don't need their arm twisted to let Joe Burrow cook, but the matchup should also push them in that direction. The matchup is also tasty for Brown. In the 2025 regular season, the Bucs allowed the most receiving yards per game (50.1) and the most yards per target (9.90) to running backs. Brown should also be leaned on as an outlet against Todd Bowles ‘ blitz-heavy tendencies. Tampa Bay had the third-highest blitz rate (35.3%) in 2025, and they've had the second-highest blitz rate (40.8%) since 2023. Meanwhile, among players on the Bengals with at least 40 routes against the blitz since 2024, Brown is tied for second in targets per route run (0.25) and has 30 targets, 23 receptions, 158 receiving yards, and 1.30 Y/RR on 122 routes against the blitz. Finally, in 23 games in which Burrow has played at least 20 snaps since 2024, Brown has tallied a 48.0% route participation rate, 11.3% target share, 0.21 TPRR, 3.7 receptions per game, 23.8 receiving yards per game, and 1.20 Y/RR. Brown should surpass those marks against Tampa Bay's pass-funnel and blitz-heavy defense, putting him over 23.5 receiving yards. We have a really fun Monday Night Football matchup for Week 1 when AFC West division rival Denver travels to Arrowhead Stadium to take on the Kansas City Chiefs. The Broncos finished 2025 one game shy of the Super Bowl after Bo Nix went down with an injury in the divisional round, and Kansas City missed the playoffs after losing Patrick Mahomes II mid-season. This game figures to be a defensive battle, given that the total is currently hovering around 43.5. There is good reason for this total as well, as both of these teams allowed fewer than 20 points per game in 2025 and each ranked inside the top six in this category. In 2025, the Chiefs and Broncos met twice, with an average of 37 points per game scored. That being said, Mahomes did not play in the second game due to a season-ending injury. Still, it is worth noting that no game in this rivalry has gone over the total of 43.5 since a New Year's Day matchup in 2023 that resulted in a 27-24 Chiefs victory. I think we could see a lot of the same tonight during the opening week of the season, as these teams have become very familiar with each other over the previous couple of seasons, and both will still be relying on strong defenses. In addition to ranking inside the top six in points per game allowed, both teams also ranked inside the top 10 in terms of total yards per game allowed. The total sits low for a reason and is certainly worth considering a play on the under. The Pick: UNDER 43.5 (-110) Monday Night Football Player Props Bo Nix OVER 16.5 rushing yards (-109) It will be hard to find props where I like taking the over tonight, but Nix's rushing yards prop is one of them. I definitely do not want to get on board with his passing yards, given the fact that Kansas City ranked eighth-best in the league in 2025 by allowing an average of just 205 passing yards per game to the quarterback position. The Chiefs did, however, allow an average of over 19 rushing yards per game to quarterbacks, which ranked in the bottom half of the league. In two games against the Chiefs, Nix carried the ball 12 times for 50 rushing yards and eclipsed this total in one of those games. BO NIX FOR THE LEAD! NYGvsDEN on CBS/Paramount+ https://t.co/HkKw7uXVnt pic.twitter.com/AQFJMRMNn4 — NFL (@NFL) October 19, 2025 Additionally, Nix rushed for 20 or more yards in nine total games, including the playoffs. He also finished the season with 25+ rushing yards in three straight games. While he is returning from a broken ankle that kept him out of the AFC Championship, all signs point to him being fully ready to go in this one. Kenneth Walker III UNDER 61.5 rushing yards (-113) I know the Chiefs are going to want to start the 2026 season by getting their new acquisition heavily involved, but this matchup against Denver may not be the best spot to do so. In 2025, Denver was stout versus the running back position, as they allowed an average of just 71.8 rushing yards per game to backs, which ranked second-best in the league. In 2025, only five running backs managed to eclipse this total against the Broncos as well. Walker certainly has the ability to get there, but against this defense, I would not bank on it. He also failed to achieve 62 rushing yards in eight total games last season. Walker was also heavily involved in the Seahawks' passing game and is expected to be utilized similarly in the Chiefs' offense. This type of utilization could take away from some carries and keep him from getting over the total here. Wil Lutz OVER 1.5 field goals made (-134) Having a game with a mid-to-low total means we have to get a bit creative in order to find some plays that hopefully cash, and that is what we are doing here with Wil Lutz for the Broncos. Lutz was quite accurate in 2025, making 28 of his 32 attempted field goals. Lutz also made two or more field goals in 10 total games last season, including the playoffs. Lutz also went 7-for-7 on field goals attempted against the Chiefs, going over 1.5 in both games. This Chiefs' defense is very much a bend-and-don't-break type of defense, which means the Broncos should have just enough success to land within field goal range on a few drives. Update: We could have some winds to contend with tonight, as the wind gusts are expected to creep up to around 30 mph according to AccuWeather. This makes this play a bit more risky, even though the game script looks promising. Monday Night Football Same Game Parlay This is a new section of the article compared to seasons past, where we will build a fun same-game parlay for you all to consider. As these are parlays, it is always recommended to scale down and make these bets a little more conservatively, as we will need multiple legs to go right in order to hit. The legs I like tonight include: Game total UNDER 49.5 Denver Broncos +8.5 RJ Harvey OVER 16.5 receiving yards Total odds: +238 (DraftKings Sportsbook) We already discussed the reasons for the under above, and it really makes sense to go ahead and tease the Broncos up to +8.5 along with the total here. I fully expect this game to be close, and quite frankly, I am not sure the better team is favored here. Both defensive units are strong, which should make for a close and low-scoring game. RJ Harvey has had a great camp, and all signs point to him having a major impact in the passing game, which is why we like him to go over 16.5 receiving yards. In 2025, Harvey was heavily involved in the passing game near the end of the season. Big-time effort by RJ Harvey to stay on his feet to pick up first down DENvsLV on CBS/Paramount+ https://t.co/HkKw7uXVnt pic.twitter.com/QQCd0aD3R3 — NFL (@NFL) December 7, 2025 Over the Broncos' final five games, including the playoffs, Harvey hauled in 19 receptions on 27 targets for 177 receiving yards and one touchdown. He also managed to eclipse this total in four of those five games. With the game expected to be close, Harvey could certainly see some dump-offs late in the game. While the Chiefs are not incredibly susceptible to receiving backs, they did allow nearly 30 receiving yards per game to running backs in 2025, and Harvey was able to eclipse this total in both games against them, hauling in eight receptions for 53 receiving yards. Moore is coming off two lackluster seasons by his standards, but a new environment and the opportunity to play with Josh Allen may have created the perfect recipe for an excellent buy-low opportunity. Moore has been seen smiling throughout training camp as he enters 2026 in a dramatically different situation after being traded from Chicago to Buffalo. Instead of playing in an environment where something was clearly not right personally and in a Ben Johnson offense where his target share declined significantly, Moore now gets to catch passes from a former MVP quarterback while reuniting with Joe Brady , his former offensive coordinator in Carolina. The biggest reason to bet Moore’s over is simple: Allen is without a doubt the best quarterback Moore has ever had passing him the ball. Moore has spent most of his career dealing with inconsistent quarterback situations, yet he has still exceeded 1,000 receiving yards in four seasons. He enters his ninth season averaging more than 1,000 receiving yards per season. Moore is also a huge upgrade at the wide receiver position for Allen. The Bills have not produced a 1,000-yard-wide receiver in either of the previous two seasons since Stefon Diggs ’ departure, while their average target depth ranked last in the NFL in 2025. Moore doesn't need an unreasonable target share to beat his season-long receiving-yardage line, but he should command a target share over 20% given the receiver depth in Buffalo. The Bills entered the 2024 season with a new slogan: Everybody Eats. Sean McDermott tried to spin that into a positive after the Bills parted ways with Diggs. However, targets are earned. The “Everybody Eats” slogan was admitting to everyone what was glaringly obvious: There wasn’t an alpha target earner on the roster. In an interview, Ian Rapoport talked about Moore as a breakout candidate for the upcoming fantasy season, but fantasy gamers should be aware that “the Buffalo Bills like to spread the ball around.” Again, this is a mythical statement and is a byproduct of a lackluster receiving room. Diggs was a member of the Buffalo Bills from 2020 to 2023. In those four years, he led all NFL receivers in receptions, was second in targets, and had 28.0% of the Bills' total team targets over that span. Before last season, Moore had four consecutive seasons in which he had over 26% of his team’s targets. In 2021, Brady’s final season as the Carolina Panthers offensive coordinator, Moore had 28.3% of the team's targets and 40.2% of the team’s total air yards. In that season, Moore caught passes from Cam Newton , Sam Darnold , and PJ Walker and still exceeded 1,150 receiving yards. The projections in the Sharp Football Analysis Draft Kit are bullish on Moore joining the Bills. Our projections have Moore projected for 83 receptions and more than 1,100 receiving yards, well over the season-long yardage prop. One of the biggest risks of betting season-long overs is injury. Moore has played every game in the past five seasons and has played 15 or more games in all eight seasons to start his career. Moore has played through injury in the past, which helps give him the opportunity to continue to accumulate volume over the full season. The market may be overreacting to Moore’s 2025 season and overconfident that his decline is age-related. In addition to our projections supporting the over, in the Wide Receiver Trends article, Rich Hribar highlighted that when searching for wide receivers to exceed expectations, one of the more common hits comes from players changing situations, making Moore a solid bet this season. For early Week 2 props, I want players with a defined role and a number they can beat without repeating their best game. That starts with a Bills quarterback hosting a Detroit defense that just allowed 410 passing yards, then moves to a pair of rushing props driven by workload. Here are the NFL props I’m targeting for Week 2. NFL Player Prop Pick: Josh Allen Passing Yards Josh Allen didn’t need big volume to carve up the Texans in Week 1. He completed 20 of 29 passes for 334 yards with two touchdowns and no interceptions in a 36-31 win at Houston. He spread the ball around, too. DJ Moore and Dalton Kincaid combined for 230 receiving yards, so Allen isn’t leaning on one target to move the offense. That makes Buffalo a tough team to slow down through the air. The Lions gave up 410 passing yards to Tyler Shough in their opener. He went 35-of-56 with three touchdowns and two interceptions, and Detroit still escaped with a 31-30 overtime win. That yardage came on a heavy workload, and Allen doesn’t need anything close to it. He threw for 334 yards on 29 attempts, which is 27 fewer than Shough. A 220.5 target leaves plenty of room. Allen can fall well short of his Week 1 performance and still cash the over, and he gets the Lions at home on Thursday night. Early Bet: Josh Allen over 220.5 passing yards NFL Player Prop Pick: Derrick Henry Rushing Yards Baltimore gave Derrick Henry plenty of work in the opener. He carried 24 times for 144 yards and three touchdowns in a 41-23 win at Indianapolis. For a yardage prop, the carries matter more than the scores. The Ravens kept feeding Henry in a game they won comfortably, and that kind of volume can get him over this number even if the big runs don’t show up. New Orleans just spent an overtime game trying to slow down Jahmyr Gibbs, without much luck. Gibbs ran 29 times for 156 yards and two touchdowns, averaging 5.4 yards per carry. Now the Saints have to deal with Henry. Henry averaged 6.0 yards per carry against the Colts, but this bet doesn’t need that kind of efficiency. Even at 4.0 per carry, 20 attempts would put him over the target. If Baltimore gives him anything close to his Week 1 volume at home on Sunday, 78.5 is a number I’m happy to bet the over on. Early Bet: Derrick Henry over 78.5 rushing yards NFL Player Prop Pick: Caleb Williams Rushing Yards Caleb Williams ran a lot more than usual in Week 1. He carried 10 times for 65 yards and two touchdowns, well above the 4.5 carries per game he averaged last season. That’s the kind of usage you want to see for a quarterback rushing prop. His 2025 numbers already support this bet. Williams finished with 77 carries for 388 yards and three touchdowns over 17 games, which works out to 22.8 rushing yards per game. The 20.5 target sits below that average before Week 1 even enters the picture. The carries could settle back down, and that’s fine. Williams averaged 5.0 yards per carry last season, so he doesn’t need double-digit attempts to reach the low 20s. With the Vikings visiting Chicago on Sunday, I’m taking the over at 20.5. His average last season was already above this target, and he ran more often in the opener.
